Use this page to declare, add, and operate the workers of a project with Compose. For the definition
of a worker, see [Workers](../understanding-iii/index#workers). For what happens when a worker
disconnects, see [Worker disconnect cleanup](../understanding-iii/engine#worker-disconnect-cleanup).

## Worker identity and namespaces

Each worker name is unique in its namespace. The engine rejects a second live worker with the same
name in the same namespace (`WORKER_NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`). See
[Namespaces](./namespaces#handle-a-rejected-registration).

`namespace:` in `worker-compose.yaml` sets the namespace of the project.
`iii compose --namespace <NS>` takes priority over it. The daemon serves `compose::*` in the same
namespace: the `--namespace` value, or else the `namespace:` of the file that the daemon starts
with. When no value is set, the namespace is `default`. See
[Compose: Precedence](./compose#precedence).

The examples on this page use the `default` namespace. When the Compose daemon runs in another
namespace, add `-n <namespace>` to each `iii trigger` and `iii compose logs` command.

## Declare workers with Compose

Project workers live under `containers:` in `worker-compose.yaml`:

```yaml
# namespace: default
engine:
  workers:
    configuration: {}
containers:
  state:
    worker: package://api.workers.iii.dev/state
    version: "0.22.2"
    config_name: state
  api:
    worker: path://./workers/api
    start_after: [state]
    scripts:
      run: pnpm start
```

A registry package needs a `version` field. The value can be an exact version, a version range, or a
tag such as `latest`. `path://` workers use `scripts.run` from the Compose file or `scripts.start`
from their `iii.worker.yaml` manifest.

Start a project and keep its daemon in the foreground:

```bash
iii compose build
iii compose --up
```

`iii compose` starts the Compose daemon. Add `--up` to also start the workers that
`worker-compose.yaml` declares.

Both commands read `worker-compose.yaml` in the working directory. To use another file, add
`--file <path>`.

`build` downloads all declared `package://` workers before startup. `--up` then reuses the shared
package cache. The command skips local `path://` workers.

With `--up`, Compose starts the engine that the `engine:` section declares and stops it when Compose
exits. When `--engine` or `III_URL` is set, Compose connects to that engine and starts no engine.
See [Which engine Compose uses](./compose#which-engine-compose-uses).

## Add a registry worker

`compose::add` resolves the worker and its registry dependencies. It adds them to
`worker-compose.yaml` and records the resolved versions in `worker-compose.lock`. A name without a
version gets the resolved version in `worker-compose.yaml`. A name with a version or a tag, such as
`queue@0.21.5`, keeps that value. Compose starts the new workers and restarts each existing worker
whose declaration changed. The other workers continue to run.

```bash
iii trigger compose::add worker=state
iii trigger compose::add worker=queue@0.21.5
```

A `worker=` value can also name a local directory, for example `worker=./workers/api`.

The call returns an `operation_id` immediately. The daemon continues the work in the background. To
see the result, run `iii trigger compose::operation operation_id=<operation_id>`. See
[Following an operation](./compose#following-an-operation).

Pass `file=/absolute/path/worker-compose.yaml` when the daemon's working directory is not the
project directory. A registry root whose kind is `engine` is rejected because the engine already
supplies it. For all request fields, see [Adding workers](./compose#adding-workers).

To find a worker, see [Worker Registry](./workers-registry).

## Operate workers

```bash
iii trigger compose::status file=worker-compose.yaml
iii compose logs state --follow
iii trigger compose::restart file=worker-compose.yaml worker=state
iii trigger compose::update file=worker-compose.yaml worker=state@latest
iii trigger compose::remove file=worker-compose.yaml worker=state
iii trigger compose::down file=worker-compose.yaml
```

`compose::restart worker=` restarts one container.

`compose::update worker=<name>` resolves the version selector that `worker-compose.yaml` declares
for that worker. An exact version stays the same. To move the worker to a different version, add a
selector, for example `worker=state@latest`. Compose restarts the project only when the package
content or the set of workers changes. See [Updating workers](./compose#updating-workers).

`compose::remove worker=` removes the worker and every reference to it from the file, then stops
that worker. Workers that were added with it stay declared. Like `compose::add`, `compose::update`
and `compose::remove` return an `operation_id` and finish in the background.

`compose::down` stops containers in reverse dependency order.

Use `engine::workers::list` and `engine::workers::info` for the engine's live connection view. Use
`compose::status` for process ownership, PID, and the last supervisor error. Use
`iii compose logs <worker> --follow` for live raw stdout and stderr.

<Note>
  To list workers, triggers, and functions, see the [iii-engine-functions worker
  docs](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/iii-engine-functions). For traces, logs, and metrics, see
  the [iii-observability worker docs](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/iii-observability).
</Note>

## Configuration

Each package ships default configuration. Use `config_name` to name the
[configuration worker](./configuration) entry for a container. Use `config_override` to change
values.

```yaml
containers:
  http:
    worker: package://api.workers.iii.dev/http
    version: "0.21.3"
    config_name: http
    config_override:
      host: 0.0.0.0
      port: 3111
```

Before Compose starts the worker, it merges the package default, the current configuration entry,
and `config_override`. `config_override` has the highest priority. Compose sends the result to the
configuration worker and does not save it. The worker reads the result with `configuration::get`,
using the id in `III_CONFIG_NAME`. See
[Configuration precedence](./compose#configuration-precedence).

## Engine-owned workers

Some workers ship with the engine. Compose does not start them as containers. To run or configure
one, put it under `engine.workers` in `worker-compose.yaml`. When an external supervisor owns the
engine, declare it in `config.yaml`. For the list of these workers, and the workers that always run,
see [Compose: Engine fields](./compose#engine-fields).

To admit untrusted workers, browsers, or agents, keep the engine port internal and add the
[rbac-proxy worker](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/rbac-proxy) with
`iii trigger compose::add worker=rbac-proxy`. It opens its own public port and applies the engine's
RBAC rules (authentication, function gating, registration hooks, filtered discovery) in front of the
existing engine port. For namespace-scoped rules, use an RBAC listener on `iii-worker-manager`. See
[Namespace-scoped function rules](../creating-workers/worker-manager#namespace-scoped-function-rules).

## Workers outside Compose

Compose is optional for a process managed by Kubernetes, systemd, another host, or an SDK-driven
development command. Give it the engine URL and a worker name. When it connects, it joins the same
trigger and function registry. Compose only owns processes declared in its file.

## Migrating an existing project

0.23 removed `iii worker`, `worker::*`, and engine-side startup of project workers. Follow the
[manual migration guide](../upgrading/workers-to-compose) before starting an older project.
